_note: Event archetypes a student-branch SPS chapter can actually run. Budgets are indicative INR for an Indian campus and assume the venue is free (own campus). `lead_weeks` is the minimum realistic runway from decision to delivery. `sps_program` names the official IEEE SPS programme that funds or supports this format, where one exists.

formats.name: Webinar / online talk
formats.notes: The cheapest way to keep a chapter visibly active and the easiest to get an international speaker for. Counts toward annual activity reporting. Record it - the recording is reusable content.
risks: Attendance drops sharply without a registration reminder 24h before
Speaker timezone mismatch

formats.name: Distinguished Lecturer visit
formats.notes: SPS maintains a roster of Distinguished Lecturers and supports chapter visits, which is how a small chapter gets a world-class speaker at low local cost. Requests go through the Society and need long lead time - apply well before the term you want.
risks: Application windows are fixed and easy to miss
Requires a confirmed date before the DL will commit

formats.name: Hands-on technical workshop
formats.notes: The workhorse format. Cap registration at the number of machines or kits you actually have. A hands-on workshop with 40 engaged participants reports better than a lecture with 200 passive ones.
risks: Lab/software setup is the usual failure point - run a full dry run
Underestimating per-participant kit cost

formats.name: Seasonal School
formats.notes: SPS funds Seasonal Schools directly and runs an annual proposal cycle - this is the single most realistic route to a large, Society-branded, Society-funded event on your campus. Proposals are competitive and need a clear theme plus committed faculty leads.
risks: Proposal cycle is annual - missing it costs a year
Residential logistics (accommodation, meals) dominate the budget

formats.name: Hackathon / datathon
formats.notes: Best co-hosted with the Computer Society or CIS chapter for turnout. A signal-processing datathon (audio, biomedical, remote sensing) differentiates you from generic app hackathons. Sponsor-friendly: prize money is the easiest thing to raise.
risks: Overnight logistics and campus security approvals
Judging criteria disputes - publish the rubric in advance

formats.name: Signal Processing Cup / VIP Cup local round
formats.sps_program: SPS Signal Processing Cup / Video & Image Processing Cup
formats.notes: SPS runs annual student competitions with a released problem and dataset. Running a campus qualifier costs almost nothing and produces teams that carry your chapter's name to the global final.
risks: Team attrition over a long project
Needs a faculty mentor committed for the whole term

formats.name: Paper-writing / reviewing bootcamp
formats.notes: Consistently one of the highest-satisfaction formats for a research-heavy campus, and cheap. Pair a senior author with a journal editor if you can reach one.
risks: Needs genuinely experienced speakers or it falls flat

formats.name: Industry visit or industry panel
formats.notes: Strong with IEEE Young Professionals as co-host. Transport is usually the whole budget. Doubles as a sponsorship conversation starter.
risks: Company NDA/security clearance delays
Cap on visitor numbers is often far lower than demand

formats.name: One-day technical symposium
formats.notes: A credible step between a workshop and a full conference, and the right thing to run first if your eventual goal is to bid to host an IEEE conference - it is the evidence a bid needs.
risks: Sponsorship shortfall
Speaker cancellations - always over-invite

formats.name: Hosting an IEEE conference / workshop on campus
formats.sps_program: SPS Call for Organizers / conference sponsorship process
formats.notes: Requires an approved conference application through IEEE (MCE), a financially responsible Organizational Unit, a General Chair with prior organising record, and a budget reviewed by IEEE. A student branch chapter realistically co-hosts with its Section and a faculty General Chair rather than leading alone.
risks: IEEE requires the financial sponsor OU to carry any loss - get Section agreement in writing early
Venue and accommodation contracts often need signing before registration income arrives
Bids are won on organiser track record; run a symposium first

formats.name: SPS Chapter Initiative project
formats.notes: SPS funds chapter-led initiatives with a social or outreach angle (rural technology access, school outreach, accessibility). Less competitive than Seasonal Schools and a strong differentiator in Section awards.
risks: Needs a genuine community partner, not just a campus event relabelled
